title: PR Senate Poll Reveals Tie Between Deltan, Curi, and Filipe
seoTitle: PR Senate Poll: Deltan, Curi, Filipe Tied for Top Spot
subtitle: Data Shows Three Candidates Tied in Race for First Senate Seat
excerpt: A Real Time Big Data poll indicates a tie between Deltan Dallagnol, Alexandre Curi, and Filipe Barros for the first Senate seat in Paraná.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
The Real Time Big Data poll, released this Friday (September 11, 2026), shows Deltan Dallagnol (Novo), Alexandre Curi (Republicanos), and Filipe Barros (PL) tied in the race for the first Senate seat in Paraná. The survey, which interviewed 1,600 voters between September 4 and 8, indicates 19% of vote intention for Deltan, 18% for Curi, and 18% for Filipe, all with a margin of error of 2 percentage points.

Tie for the First PR Senate Seat

The poll, with a 95% confidence level, recorded the percentages of 1st and 2nd votes, reflecting the consolidated choices of voters. Curi and Filipe each have 18%, while Deltan reaches 19%, placing the three candidates above Gleisi Hoffmann (PT) and Cristina Graeml (PSD), who register 16% and 14%, respectively.

Context of RPC Interviews

In the same week, RPC, a TV Globo affiliate, aired interviews with the nine candidates for the Senate in Paraná. The top five, according to the Quaest poll, participated in 30-minute live question-and-answer sessions, while the others presented their proposals on Saturday. Alexandre Curi, for example, advocated for ending the 6x1 work schedule with tax compensation for micro and small businesses.

Candidates' Stances

Deltan Dallagnol stated he is eligible despite pending registration with the Electoral Court. Filipe Barros emphasized increasing penalties for femicide and serving sentences in maximum-security prisons. Gleisi Hoffmann advocated for opening impeachment proceedings against STF ministers in cases of irregularities.

Other Topics in Debate

Among the agendas presented, notable points include Dr. Rosinha's proposal for a Misogyny Law, Karen Guerreiro's advocacy for more specialist doctors in the interior, and Marcelo Marcelino's intention to re-nationalize privatized companies, citing Copel and Sanepar.

Poll Data and Methodology

The poll cost R$ 24,000.00, financed by its own resources, and is registered with the Superior Electoral Court under number PR-08220/2026. The complete data, in a 2 MB PDF, is available for download on the Poder360 website.

With information from Poder360, G1.
